texts.preamble: Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Before The Court Of Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At Bangalore (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Satish J.Bali, B.Com., Ll.M., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes (Scch-16) Bangalore. Dated This The 11th Day Of July 2016. MVC.No.2878/2013 ** ** Petitioner: Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P., S/o Marria Siluvai Pitchai, Aged about 41 years, Recently residing at G22 block, 12th Cross, Krishnareddy Garden, Doddanekkundi, Bangalore - 37. Permanently residing at No.1/55, Old Mahabilipuram road, Chemmeny Cherry, Ch 19, Amma Ds, Chennai - 600 119. (Sri M. Subramani, Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. M/s. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Policy No.OG-13-1701-1803- 2 Mvc 2878/13 Sch-16 00007041 valid from 16-02-2013 to 15-02-2014. (Sri M.B. Ravikumar, Advocate) Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. texts.facts: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident happened on 29-04-2013 at about 4.15 p.m. 2. The brief facts of the petition averments are as under: On the above said date and time, the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-U-2463 on left side of the road from Bellandur towards Marathahalli slowly and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations. When he was proceeding near Kadubisanahalli fly over, at that time, the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03- AA-1996 came in a rash and negligent manner, without following traffic rules and regulations and came in opposite direction on one way and suddenly took right turn without observing movements of the vehicles and dashed to the SCH-16 petitioner motor cycle, because of which the petitioner sustained communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal, laceration left index finger, abrasions all over the body. He was immediately admitted to VIMS Hospital, wherein first aid was given. Thereafter, he admitted as an inpatient from 29- 04-2013 to 01-05-2013, during the said period, the petitioner underwent ORIF left 3rd metacarpal and wound debridement and suturing of index finger. The petitioner was discharged with an advice of follow up treatment. 3. It is further case of the petitioner that, he has spent considerable amount towards his treatment and he has to bear other expenses for removal of implants. It is stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and partner at Chef Baker's at Doddnekkundi, Bangalore and earning Rs.50,000/- per month. Due to the impact of the said accident, the petitioner became permanently disabled and not able to earn anything. The jurisdictional police have registered a case against the driver of the above said offending car in their Crime No.46/2013 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC. The first respondent being the owner of the above said car and second respondent being SCH-16 the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Hence, prayed to allow the petition. 4. In response to the notice, the second respondent appeared, whereas first respondent was placed exparte, as he failed to appear before the court in spite of service of notice. 5. The respondent No.2 admitted that, it had issued policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996 and it was valid from 16-02-2013 to 15-02-2014. The respondent No.2 denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the manner of accident. The respondent No.2 contended that, the driver of the above said car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and was not qualified for holding such a driving licence. The owner of the said vehicle has been knowing fully handed over the position of the said vehicle to the driver who did not possessed valid and effective driving licence. It is contended that, the driver of the above said car was in the Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184882940/ 2 influence of alcohol and the respondent No.1 immediately after the accident has not intimated about the accident and jurisdictional police have not supplied necessary vehicle documents. Thereby, there is a violation of Section 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act. The respondent No.2 denied SCH-16 the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also expenses incurred by the petitioner towards his treatment. It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that, the petitioner without observing traffic rules and regulations has proceeded on his motor cycle because of which, the accident took place. It is contended that, the owner and insurer of the motor cycle of the petitioner are also necessary parties. The respondent No.2 further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant, without any basis. Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition with costs. 7. The petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15. Per contra, the respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence.
texts.arguments: Relying upon a judgment of the Apex Court reported in 2013 AIR SCW 5375 (Minu Rout and others Vs. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra and others), with regard to interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the compensation amount, in para 13 of the judgment, the Apex Court held that Insurance Company is also liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% p.a. SCH-16 from the date of application till the date of payment and also by following the principles laid down in (2011) 4 SCC 481 : (AIR 2012 SC 100) (Municipal Council of Delhi Vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy).
